note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

points: Israel did evil and the Lord delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years, so they made dens in the mountains and caves and strongholds; Midian and Amalek and the children of the east destroyed the increase of the earth and left no sustenance, no sheep, nor ox, nor ass, and Israel was greatly impoverished.

note.label: Book of Our Fathers: Who’s Who Part 3

points: Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years. That is our manner: the Most High delivers us, we get a little bit of freedom, and we go right back to wickedness. The same thing goes on today; we get relaxed, and the Lord has to remind us, putting us right back into hard bondage, that this is not our rest.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: Because of the Midianites, the children of Israel made them the dens in the mountains, and caves, and strongholds; Israel hid in the mountains of their own land.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: When Israel had sown, the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the children of the east came up as grasshoppers for multitude, destroyed the increase of the earth, and left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass, and Israel was greatly impoverished. That goes right into the curses.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: When Israel cried unto the Lord, the Lord sent a prophet to remind them: I brought you up from Egypt out of the house of bondage, and I said, fear not the gods of the Amorites in whose land ye dwell, but ye have not obeyed my voice. The judgment came with a reason attached.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: The Lord commissions him: go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites; have not I sent thee? Gideon answers with his pedigree: my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house. That is a defeated mentality, and we all have to overcome it, because every one of us was called for a reason, to put a brick in for the kingdom.

Rich, poor, or middle class, none of it matters to the Most High; what man holds in high esteem, God calls abomination. The highest calling anyone can have on the face of the earth is to teach the word of God and compel the lost sheep of the house of Israel to come in, so do not think less of yourself because your name carries no prestige.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

points: The Lord tells Gideon the people with him are too many for him to give Midian into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against him, saying, mine own hand hath saved me. That is Israel: look at what I did. The Lord knows how we think.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

points: The men of Israel ask Gideon to rule over them, both he, his son, and his son's son, for delivering them from the hand of Midian. Israel has always needed a leader, because we are lost sheep; we need somebody to guide us in the way we must go, or we wander off the path of righteousness. It has always been that way, and you see it playing out right here.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Gideon made an ephod thereof and put it in his city, even in Ophrah: and all Israel went thither a whoring after it, which thing became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Thus was Midian subdued before the children of Israel, so that they lifted up their heads no more, and the country was in quietness forty years in the days of Gideon. Gideon had threescore and ten sons, for he had many wives, and his concubine in Shechem bare him a son whose name he called Abimelech; and Gideon the son of Joash died in a good old age.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: It came to pass, as soon as Gideon was dead, that the children of Israel turned again, and went a whoring after Baalim, and made Baal-berith their god, and remembered not the Lord their God, who had delivered them out of the hands of all their enemies on every side; neither shewed they kindness to the house of Jerubbaal.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: After Abimelech there arose to defend Israel Tola the son of Puah, a man of Issachar; he judged Israel twenty and three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir.
Notice it says to defend Israel. Israel was in the land, but do not forget that the Lord had left nations among us, so the judges had to defend the people.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the LORD. That is the cycle of this whole book: after a judge died and Israel had peace and safety for a while, the people went right back into their sin, just like always.

Israel served Baalim and Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria, the gods of Zidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines, and forsook the LORD, and served not him. Ashtaroth is Ishtar or Astarte, the so called queen of heaven; the heathen carried the same goddess under different names, the same one the Greeks called Aphrodite.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The anger of the LORD was hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hands of the Philistines and into the hands of the children of Ammon. Israel was serving their gods, so the Lord sold Israel to them.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: Eighteen years they vexed and oppressed all the children of Israel that were on the other side Jordan, in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead: that was Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh in their allotments across the river.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: Moreover the children of Ammon passed over Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, which shows those tribes dwelling in their own allotments on the other side; so that Israel was sore distressed.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The children of Israel cried unto the LORD, saying, We have sinned against thee, both because we have forsaken our God, and also served Baalim. The enemy had destroyed on one side of Jordan and was crossing over against Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim, so now Israel wanted to confess.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The children of Israel said unto the LORD, We have sinned: do thou unto us whatsoever seemeth good unto thee; deliver us only, we pray thee, this day. And they put away the strange gods from among them and served the LORD. This time the repentance came with action.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: And his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel. The Most High loves Israel; it grieved him to have his own children in captivity, but he cannot break his word, so the repentance had to come first. That is also why Christ was sent to die for our sins, so we could have a chance to return to him in the last days.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: The children of Ammon were gathered together and encamped in Gilead, and the children of Israel assembled themselves together and encamped in Mizpeh.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

points: In process of time the children of Ammon made war against Israel, and the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah out of the land of Tob: come and be our captain, that we may fight with the children of Ammon. Now they wanted the man of valour they had cast out.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: The king of Ammon answered, Because Israel took away my land, when they came up out of Egypt, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and unto Jordan: now therefore restore those lands again peaceably. That claim was a lie, and Jephthah knew it.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Jephthah sent messengers again and broke down the whole history: Israel took not away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon. He knew the record, so nobody could talk him out of it.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Then Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon: let us pass, we pray thee, through thy land into my place. But Sihon trusted not Israel to pass through his coast; he gathered all his people together, pitched in Jahaz, and fought against Israel. They came against Israel; Israel did nothing to them.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: And the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and from the wilderness even unto Jordan. That is how Israel got the land of the Amorites: the Lord gave it in battle when they came out against his people.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: So now the LORD God of Israel hath dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel, and shouldest thou possess it? The Lord moved the Amorites out by moving Israel in; why should Ammon possess what the Most High gave to Israel?

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Art thou any thing better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? did he ever strive against Israel, or did he ever fight against them? While Israel dwelt in Heshbon and her towns, and in Aroer and her towns, and in all the cities along the coasts of Arnon, three hundred years, why did ye not recover them within that time? Three hundred years Israel held that land and nobody came to claim it.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Wherefore I have not sinned against thee, but thou doest me wrong to war against me: the LORD the Judge be judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon. The Lord is in the midst of every battle; nothing goes down without the Most High letting it go down. World War One, the Lord was in the midst; World War Two, the Lord was in the midst; whoever he has destined to win is going to win.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: The Lord gave him the victory he asked for and Ammon was subdued before Israel.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: Jephthah passed over unto the children of Ammon to fight against them, and the LORD delivered them into his hands. He smote them from Aroer even till thou come to Minnith, even twenty cities, with a very great slaughter. Thus the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Jephthah did not burn his daughter as a human sacrifice. Israel did not do human sacrifices; that was Molech worship among the Canaanites. Read the end of the passage: at the end of two months she returned unto her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed, and she knew no man. If she had been put to death, there would be no reason for the scripture to say she knew no man; her life was committed to the Lord and she remained a virgin.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Why would she mourn her virginity if she were about to die? Because the sorrow was that she could never marry or bear children. In those days our women wanted to bring children into the world and continue the lineage; to be without children was counted a shame and a dishonour among the daughters of Israel.
And it was a custom in Israel, that the daughters of Israel went yearly to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: Jephthah judged Israel six years; then died Jephthah the Gileadite, and was buried in one of the cities of Gilead.

note.label: Judges 12: Strife Amongst Brethren

points: After him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel. He had thirty sons and thirty daughters, whom he sent abroad, and took in thirty daughters from abroad for his sons. He judged Israel seven years, and died, and was buried at Bethlehem.

note.label: Judges 12: Strife Amongst Brethren

points: After him Elon, a Zebulonite, judged Israel ten years; and Elon the Zebulonite died, and was buried in Aijalon in the country of Zebulun.

note.label: Judges 12: Strife Amongst Brethren

points: After him Abdon the son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, judged Israel. He had forty sons and thirty nephews, that rode on threescore and ten ass colts; and he judged Israel eight years, and died, and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the mount of the Amalekites.

note.label: Judges 12: Strife Amongst Brethren

points: The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years. This is the pattern of the book of Judges: after Joshua's death Israel went off, and nation after nation was given power over them before the great captivities ever came.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: No razor was to come on his head, for the child would be a Nazarite unto God from the womb, and he would begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines. This is one of the first examples in scripture of somebody actually living the vow that was laid out in Numbers 6.
The locks of the Nazarite also witness to who Israel is; the hair of Israel naturally grows into locks.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: His father and his mother knew not that it was of the Lord, that he sought an occasion against the Philistines, for at that time the Philistines had dominion over Israel. The Lord was moving Samson's spirit, and the parents did not understand, just as we often question the Most High when we have no idea the depths of his wisdom and what he is really doing.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

points: Samson judged Israel in the days of the Philistines twenty years; he ended up a leadership figure, a judge over Israel.

note.label: Judges 15: The Jawbone of an Ass

points: His brethren and all the house of his father came down and took him, and brought him up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the buryingplace of Manoah his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.

note.label: Judges 16: Samson and Delilah

points: This verse is the key to understanding the whole book of Judges. With no king and no government, Israel was sheep without a shepherd, and when you see how the people carry on in these chapters, that is why: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.

The same individual spirit is around today in those who say join no camp and let no man teach you. Every time the scripture shows Israel without a leadership structure, all manner of wickedness follows, primarily idolatry.

note.label: Judges 17: Micah's House of Idols and the Hired Levite

points: Again the scripture reiterates there was no king in Israel. In those days the tribe of the Danites was still seeking an inheritance to dwell in, because unto that day all their inheritance had not fallen unto them among the tribes; they had conquered in Joshua's day but never attained all their land.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: When the priest saw them coming out with the gods and asked, what do ye? they told him hold thy peace, lay thine hand upon thy mouth: is it better for thee to be a priest unto the house of one man, or unto a tribe and a family in Israel? Do not snitch; roll with us and be the man over a whole tribe.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: They built the city again, dwelt therein, and called the name of it Dan, after Dan their father which was born unto Israel; howbeit the name of the city was Laish at the first.

note.label: Judges 18: Dan Steals Micah's Gods and Takes Laish

points: Once more, there was no king in Israel, no leadership structure, still sheep without a shepherd. A certain Levite sojourning on the side of mount Ephraim took to him a concubine out of Bethlehemjudah; a concubine was a woman dealt with on the level of a servant.

note.label: Judges 19: The Levite's Concubine at Gibeah

points: When the servant suggested turning in to lodge in this city of the Jebusites, his master refused: we will not turn aside hither into the city of a stranger, that is not of the children of Israel; we will pass over to Gibeah. Even in those wild days he would not lodge with heathens, only with his brothers.

note.label: Judges 19: The Levite's Concubine at Gibeah

points: When he was come into his house he took a knife, laid hold on his concubine, and divided her, together with her bones, into twelve pieces, and sent her into all the coasts of Israel, to make the twelve tribes aware of what was done in Gibeah.

note.label: Judges 19: The Levite's Concubine at Gibeah

points: All that saw it said, there was no such deed done nor seen from the day that the children of Israel came up out of the land of Egypt unto this day: consider of it, take advice, and speak your minds. The nation had never seen a matter like this, and it called the whole congregation to counsel.

note.label: Judges 19: The Levite's Concubine at Gibeah

points: All the children of Israel went out, and the congregation was gathered together as one man, from Dan even to Beersheba, with the land of Gilead, unto the LORD in Mizpeh: four hundred thousand footmen that drew sword.

Israel got ready for war behind one woman, one victim. There is no hatred of women in this truth; wicked women are rebuked, which is itself love, and here a crime against one sister moved the whole nation to arms.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: He said they have committed lewdness and folly in Israel. Nowhere in the Bible can rape be called lawful; it is lewdness and folly, and whether the victim lives or dies the matter is counted as murder. Be very mindful of sick, perverted camps that teach otherwise.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: They set an order for war, ten men of an hundred throughout all the tribes to fetch victual for the people, and all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man. Even wicked and without a king, Israel had some morals left; gang rape was intolerable.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: The tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, what wickedness is this that is done among you? Now deliver us the men, the children of Belial which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death and put away evil from Israel; everything those men had going on was worthy of death.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: Judges is talking about the civil war; some of you do not know we had a civil war in Israel. History recounted in class: in Judges 19 the men of Gibeah of Benjamin abused a man's wife until she died, he sent the evidence of it to the rest of the tribes, and all the tribes rose up against Benjamin.
The children of Benjamin gathered themselves together out of the cities unto Gibeah, to go out to battle against the children of Israel.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: But the children of Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of their brethren; instead they gathered themselves together out of the cities unto Gibeah to go out to battle against the children of Israel, riding for their own no matter the crime.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: The men of Israel beside Benjamin were four hundred thousand men of war that drew sword. Four hundred thousand against twenty and six thousand: you would think a landslide victory.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: The children of Israel arose, went up to the house of God, and asked counsel of God: which of us shall go up first to the battle against the children of Benjamin? And the LORD said, Judah shall go up first.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: Israel encamped against Gibeah and put themselves in array, and the children of Benjamin came forth out of Gibeah and destroyed down to the ground of the Israelites that day twenty and two thousand men. Benjamin opened the battle by giving Judah the business.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: The men of Israel encouraged themselves; we cannot go out like that to the men of Gibeah. They set their battle again in array in the same place, went up and wept before the LORD until even, and asked, shall I go up again to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother? And the LORD said, go up against him.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: Then all the children of Israel and all the people went up unto the house of God, wept, sat there before the LORD, fasted that day until even, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD. This time the whole nation humbled itself.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: Now Israel set liers in wait round about Gibeah. No more going head up against lefthanded slingers you cannot beat straight on; now there was a strategy, an ambush.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: Part of Israel put themselves in array as at other times, and Benjamin was drawn away from the city, beginning to smite and kill about thirty men and saying, they are smitten down before us as at the first. Little did they know they were falling into the plan; Israel fled on purpose and drew them from the city onto the highways.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: The Lord smote Benjamin before Israel, and the children of Israel destroyed of the Benjamites that day 25,100 men. In that civil war 25,000 of us died in a day.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: The liers in wait came forth out of their places, even out of the meadows of Gibeah, ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and the LORD smote Benjamin before Israel: the children of Israel destroyed of the Benjamites that day twenty and five thousand and an hundred men. The victory belonged to the Most High, as he had promised.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: There was an appointed sign between the men of Israel and the liers in wait, that they should make a great flame with smoke rise up out of the city. That was the purpose of drawing the Benjamites out: while Benjamin smote about thirty men and thought they were winning as in the first battles, the liers in wait hasted, rushed upon Gibeah, smote all the city with the edge of the sword, and set the sign.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: Six hundred men turned and fled to the wilderness unto the rock Rimmon and abode there four months; only that remnant kept the tribe from being utterly destroyed. The men of Israel turned again upon the children of Benjamin and smote them with the edge of the sword, men of every city, and beast, and all that came to hand, and set on fire all the cities they came to.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: The men of Israel had sworn at Mizpeh that not one of them would give his daughter unto Benjamin to wife. This follows the previous chapter, where the tribes went to war against Benjamin.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: The children of Israel repented them for Benjamin their brother, for there was one tribe cut off from Israel that day. They had also made a great oath that whoever came not up to the Lord at Mizpeh would surely be put to death.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: The people repented them for Benjamin because the Lord had made a breach in the tribes of Israel, and the elders said there must be an inheritance for them that be escaped of Benjamin, that a tribe be not destroyed out of Israel.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: Verse 18 restates why they could not just give their own daughters: the children of Israel had sworn, saying, Cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin. That is the same oath read in verse 7.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: The children of Israel departed thence at that time, every man to his tribe, to his family, and to his inheritance.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes. We see that same thing today: most of our people are still in that state, doing what is right in their own eyes. There is nothing new under the sun.

note.label: Judges 21: The Oath at Mizpeh and Wives for Benjamin

points: “In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.” Everybody doing whatever the hell they want. That's Christianity today. You're under grace, not under the law; don't worry, God won't do anything to you. Turn the sisters into hoes and single mothers and God will forgive you. That's not in the Bible.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

points: The Lord recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust. Ruth answered, Let me find favour in thy sight, my lord, for thou hast comforted me, though I be not like unto one of thine handmaidens.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing: for to confirm all things, a man plucked off his shoe and gave it to his neighbour, and this was a testimony in Israel. So the kinsman said unto Boaz, Buy it for thee, and he drew off his shoe.

note.label: Ruth 4: Boaz Redeems the Inheritance

points: All the people that were in the gate and the elders said, We are witnesses. They blessed the marriage: the Lord make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel; and let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare unto Judah, of the seed which the Lord shall give thee of this young woman.

note.label: Ruth 4: Boaz Redeems the Inheritance

points: Eli told her, Go in peace, and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition: God heard her prayers and her countenance was no more sad.

note.label: Mind Control & The Power Of Prayer

points: This is how the Lord took care of Levi. He told Levi in the law that Levi would have no inheritance of land among the tribes; the Lord provided for them through the sacrifices that Israel brought, so they had need of nothing.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Now Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel. See, he heard what his sons did unto all Israel. Good.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel, and how they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: the harlots hanging around the temple, and Eli's sons dealing with them.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: There came a man of God unto Eli, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh's house? That is talking about Levi, going into Moses. Did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel? They had need of nothing; they were well taken care of.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: And honourest thy sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel my people. That is the error that some fathers and mothers make. You honour your children above the Lord, and now you end up in jail, beat up, or dead.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me? You are disrespecting me, is what he is saying: I am supposed to be honoured in everything before the children of Israel, and you let your sons disrespect my offerings.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: Wherefore the Lord God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the Lord saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed. Lightly esteemed means the Lord is not really looking out for you: you are not thinking about me, so I am not thinking about you; go ahead and see how it works out for yourself.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

points: And the Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house. Because he warned Eli, his sons were wicked. So now he is telling Samuel, I am about to destroy Eli.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: The Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end. For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not. Eli let his children break the commandments of the Lord and lead the people astray, and he restrained them not.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord. And the Lord appeared again in Shiloh: for the Lord revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

points: The word of Samuel came to all Israel, and Israel went out against the Philistines to battle, pitching beside Ebenezer while the Philistines pitched in Aphek. The Philistines never wanted to leave Israel alone.

note.label: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken

points: When they joined battle, Israel was smitten before the Philistines, and about four thousand men of the army fell in the field. The Philistines came up against us and whooped us in this first battle.

note.label: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken

points: The elders of Israel asked the right question, Wherefore hath the Lord smitten us to day before the Philistines? But instead of examining the nation, they had an idea: fetch the ark of the covenant out of Shiloh, and when it comes among us it will save us out of the hand of our enemies.

note.label: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken

points: Tobit's charge to his son: beware of all whoredom, take a wife of the seed of thy fathers and not a strange woman, for Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob all married wives of their own kindred and their seed shall inherit the land.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father's tribe: for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred. What did they do? Married wives of their own kindred. And were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.

note.label: Unity: The Sweet Savor Of Salvation

points: For we are the children of the prophets: Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, including Noah. Noah didn't marry daughters of men; he married his own kind, a daughter of God, and his sons' wives are their own kind. Noah did not step outside of that. He did not do what the sons of God were doing, go out and mess with Cain's daughters. He was like, nah, I'mma keep the laws of God and marry my own.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father's tribe. The Most High calls marrying a strange woman whoredom. We are the children of the prophets Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; our fathers from the beginning all married wives of their own kindred and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.
